scope: Reviewed implementation coverage, not a claim of end-to-end Kepler parity. Adapter presence does not mean the sandbox exposes that workflow.

capabilities.title: Point
capabilities.foundation: Native resident point fields, color/size scales, categorical palettes, analysis override, fill/outline and original-row picking verified in browser; native point XYZ altitude, pitched picking, XY/XYZ toggles, range filtering, portable replay and completed-stream handoff verified; bounded native scalar bitmap labels with visible glyphs, source-aligned masks, labels-only rendering and stable glyph buffers on display changes verified in browser
capabilities.gap: Hover-neighbor display (showNeighborOnHover, LAYERS4-A, browser-unverified) reads the neighbors list column; its overlay uses constant radius and highlight/layer color, not native per-row channels. Multi-value labels: each native textLabel entry is its own independent label layer (verified by node spec; native does no stacking and several fields per entry exist only for tooltips); each entry costs its own atlas. Column modes geojson, geoarrow and neighbors have no resident binding. Labels remain bitmap text (SDF only with an outline); collision runs on the CPU up to 100k rows (Mercator) and on the GPU (Mercator and globe) above it or without CPU anchors. Remaining: browser qualification of brushing, labels and neighbors.
capabilities.acceptance: Native style changes, filtered drawing and source-row picking agree.

capabilities.title: Arc
capabilities.foundation: Native Arc override with resident endpoint geometry, filtered rendering and source-row identity; native visual-channel planner; GlobeView great-circle strokes and target arrowheads verified in browser
capabilities.gap: Native Arc has no altitude and only target-end arrowheads; source/both-end arrowheads and arc altitude are not native and stay unsupported. Neighbor and GeoArrow column modes report specific unsupported reasons. Remaining: browser qualification of width/color channel combinations. No implementable native gap found in LAYERS4.
capabilities.acceptance: Native arc configuration and source identities match across filtering.

capabilities.title: Line
capabilities.foundation: Native Line rendering and same-ID type changes; filtered endpoints, GPU target gradients/alpha and original-row picking; GlobeView great-circle strokes and target arrowheads verified in browser
capabilities.gap: Altitude columns must exist at prepare time; native Arc-style altitude is refused and native has only target-end arrowheads. Remaining: 3D line renderer and browser qualification of channel combinations (all unverified on WebGPU).
capabilities.acceptance: Native line controls either render correctly or give a specific unsupported reason.

capabilities.title: Grid
capabilities.foundation: Native Grid override; scoped GPU aggregation, cell rendering and bounded cell inspection. Implemented, not yet browser-qualified: all ten native aggregations (GPUGroupStatistics), elevation channel with enable3d extrusion, color/elevation percentile cutoffs, quantize/quantile/linear/custom scales (aggregation-statistics-*.ts).
capabilities.gap: LAYERS4-B (GPU spec and node spec written, GPU spec not run): bin order now follows native first appearance (GPU min-source-row per cell) for categorical scales, dictionary labels come from the reconciled global dictionary, and count labels are drawn through native renderCountLabels (browser-unverified, needs viewport, globe untested). LAYERS5: bin order now follows the native bin-forming rows (the layer topology mask, CPU filters and polygons) while values honour the GPU-filter display mask, so a filter hiding the first row of a bin no longer reorders bins (headless GPU spec aggregation-bin-order.spec.ts, 4 tests pass locally; applies to the fixture and published datasets, not point-variant aggregation); the first-appearance remap sorts representative cells on the GPU and supports dictionaries up to 4,194,304 labels (two dictionary-sized scratch arrays are not in the program memory preflight). Limits: categorical mode ties resolve to the smallest code; sums use fixed point; quantile thresholds are f32; extrusion lighting not visually compared. Qualify projection and boundary cases.
capabilities.acceptance: Cell assignments, count/sum/mean, empty cells and picked aggregate IDs match a reference.

capabilities.title: Hexbin
capabilities.foundation: Native Hexagon override; planar cell assignment, scoped GPU aggregation and filtered host rendering. Implemented, not yet browser-qualified: all ten native aggregations, elevation channel with enable3d extrusion, percentile cutoffs, quantize/quantile/linear/custom scales (shared aggregation-statistics-*.ts with Grid).
capabilities.gap: Same as Grid (LAYERS4-B): GPU first-appearance bin order, global dictionary labels and native count labels are implemented but unrun in a browser. Same LAYERS5 bin-order changes and limits (variant aggregation still orders by the display mask, dictionaries above 4,194,304 labels use raw code order), mode tie rule, lighting not compared. Qualify geographic boundary and drilldown cases.
capabilities.acceptance: Pinned boundary/tie cases and aggregate identities pass; overflow is visible.

capabilities.title: Polygon and GeoJSON
capabilities.foundation: Published mixed GeoJSON and Arrow geometry, holes/multipolygons, chunked feature identity, native field styles and embedded color/width/radius properties; GlobeView polygons, outlines, extrusion, paths and points verified in browser
capabilities.gap: Globe edge subdivision (linear lon/lat at 5/2/1 degree bands, antimeridian unwrap, per-cell polygon cuts) and native extrusion/outline/wireframe/height logic already exist; LAYERS4-C added native rounded caps and joints for paths and outlines (browser-unverified). Limits: non-EPSG:4326/CRS84 geometry is refused (native has no CRS handling); globe edges are not great-circle subdivided and pole-encircling polygons keep source longitudes; globe variants and rounded caps unverified in a browser. Remaining geometry encodings and boundary cases need qualification.
capabilities.acceptance: Holes, multipolygons, selection and picking remain aligned to source features.

capabilities.title: Cluster
capabilities.foundation: Exact native supercluster at every size (no row cap): positions, filter mask and aggregation field are read back in accounted 8 MiB slices and a module Web Worker builds the pinned supercluster index with native getClusterer options; all native aggregations (including min/max/median) run through native aggregate(). Positions are float32 from the GPU, so parity is against supercluster fed the same float32 values.
capabilities.gap: The CPU reservation is now measured: supercluster is ported to a typed-array index built in the worker (exact order/centers/members parity, node-tested) with an initial 160 bytes/row budget that retries up to 512 bytes/row and shrinks to about 52 bytes/row plus measured hierarchy after the build. LAYERS5: the index is built lazily and now skips zoom levels where nothing can merge: only levels down to the viewed zoom are built (zooming out extends the index in the worker and admits the extra bytes, a budget miss triggers a rebuild with a doubled budget), measured on 400k random rows at zoom 14: global spread 2428 ms to 399 ms, dense city spread unchanged (about 1.5 s, merging starts at fine zooms) - all in the worker, exact parity with supercluster by node spec. This is NOT a GPU cluster index: positions, mask and field are still read back, every mask or radius change rebuilds the tree on the CPU (no incremental update), per-cluster field aggregation still runs on the main thread, and a GPU hierarchy cannot be exactly equivalent. Reservation numbers are estimates, no browser run: zoom redraw, hover popover, teardown and the budget-retry path (no runtime spec) remain unverified.
capabilities.acceptance: Browser: check-cluster-native.mjs asserts exact parity with supercluster at 300,000 rows (counts, order, centers, member sets, sum/average/min/max/median) at several zooms, minClusterSize and filter masks.

capabilities.title: Icon
capabilities.foundation: Native SVG mesh catalog with source-preserving grouping, GPU position/style/mask gathers, original-row picking and stable buffers across filtering; fixed and scaled radius verified
capabilities.gap: Altitude, text labels and portable custom catalogs are implemented but browser-unverified (LAYERS-40..43). LAYERS5: icon labels now pad by the per-row size channel like native getTextOffsetByRadius (the source-aligned size vector is passed to the label layer; label collision still treats variable radii as zero, as for points); node/GPU unrun in a browser. Wide-icon globe probe unqualified.
capabilities.acceptance: Catalog failures are visible and filtered icons pick the correct source rows.

capabilities.title: Heatmap
capabilities.foundation: Planar native WebGPU SUM/MEAN heatmap, radius and Float32 weight fields with linear/square-root/log DOMAIN normalization; ordered GPU masks/weights/density, native controls, nullable batches and stable source/output buffers verified
capabilities.gap: No further native weight scales exist (linear, sqrt, log only). Native heatmaps are pickable:false with no brushing, so brushing and row picking remain unsupported extensions. Admission requires blendable rgba16float at 512x512. Globe uses a data-bounds density frame on a tessellated sphere. Qualify projection/zoom, extreme-density and export combinations; no GLSL parity claim.
capabilities.acceptance: GPU oracles match pinned WebGPU density, maximum and final pixels. Native browser verifies constant/weighted SUM/MEAN, radius, linear/sqrt/log scales, independent display/domain selections, empty replay and unchanged source buffers/uploads.

capabilities.title: H3
capabilities.foundation: Exact Uint64/string cell IDs, batch-preserving geometry, native polygon/viewport-column branches, coverage, topology filters and original-row picking; actual browser verified stable source buffers and pan-cache behavior; GlobeView uses the polygon branch like native Deck and is verified in browser
capabilities.gap: LAYERS4-B: extruded cells use the native white 3D highlight and flat cells draw a native-style hovered-outline PathLayer (skipped with a size field); implemented, browser-unverified. Native has no hierarchy ops. fp64: hi/lo split paths exist (see LAYERS2/3) but low parts only matter in LNGLAT offset mode at high zoom, shaders have never run on a GPU, points/lines/arcs have no low stream, globe stays Float32.
capabilities.acceptance: Cell identity and value lookup survive mixed resolutions and filtering.

capabilities.title: Scenegraph
capabilities.foundation: Kepler scenegraph and Deck mesh loaders; Deck 9.4 ScenegraphLayer/SimpleMeshLayer carry WGSL (audited by node spec, no GLSL-only injection found)
capabilities.gap: Scenegraph sublayers of the synthetic 3D tile are inspected by scripts/tile3d-effects.mjs (transforms, resource release after removal; verified 2026-10-31, tile3d-effects.mjs exit 0). Kepler's simple-phong override for PBR layers is ported (shadow module useSimplePhong with pbrMaterial unlit, applied by WGSLShadowLightingEffect when shadow lights exist; compile-checked by wgsl-shadow-scenegraph.spec.ts, no pixel comparison against Kepler); PBR materials, glTF animations and picking are not browser-verified.
capabilities.acceptance: Model loading, transforms, picking and resource cleanup pass in the pinned host.

capabilities.title: Trips
capabilities.foundation: Explicit timed LineString and grouped tabular (ID/time/lon/lat) source preparation, native Trips animation/trails, GPU masks/style gathers, member-row filtering, picking and saved timestamp settings; scenegraph markers (gallery/custom glTF) drawn by Deck's ScenegraphLayer, so model textures, PBR materials (native `_lighting: 'pbr'`) and glTF animations (native speed 5) render, with compute-evaluated GPU position and heading, roll/pitch/yaw datum fields and per-timestamp table-mode colors read from resident per-vertex columns, size/adjust/model angles, invert flags and color
capabilities.gap: Globe markers: no code path rejects them and the heading is the native Mercator speed-vector yaw, and the globe scenario of scripts/trip-markers.mjs exit 0 (verified 2026-10-31; trips-grouped.mjs also exit 0). Datum fields accept Float32, Int8/16/32, UInt8/16/32 (widened on the GPU, exact within 2^24) and, under the explicit prepare precision policy, Float64, Int64, UInt64 and Decimal narrowed to Float32 (loss beyond the error budget is rejected); these conversions and the budget growth below are node-spec verified only (backlog FLOW3-T-1/T-2). Like native (GeoJSON-mode trips carry no datum), datums apply to grouped tabular trips only. Marker orientation needs the resident filtered-trip channels; a large grouped trip now grows its working budget to its exact output bytes plus a quarter of headroom, bounded by the free dataset-registry memory, and only falls back to trails with a reason when the registry itself cannot hold it. Native has no multipart timed trajectories, so none are provided.
capabilities.acceptance: Time boundaries, trail length, pause/seek and picking match source trips.

capabilities.title: S2
capabilities.foundation: Exact Uint64/hex-token decoding at publication from BigInt (no Float64); Deck-equivalent curved-edge footprints with continuous antimeridian longitudes as derived geoarrow.wkb polygons beside the unchanged ID field; batches, empty batches and null rows preserved; style, domain, selection masks and original-row picking reuse the resident polygon path; node tests cover all six faces and mixed levels against s2-geometry
capabilities.gap: Rendered as derived polygon footprints through the resident GeoJSON renderer (Float32 coordinates), not browser-verified. Native s2/a5/geohash layers have no hierarchy or parent/child operations (checked in LAYERS4), so none are planned; fill/stroke/size/height channels, 3D and wireframe depend on the shared polygon path and need qualification.
capabilities.acceptance: Mixed levels, antimeridian cells and stable picking pass in the pinned browser.

capabilities.title: A5
capabilities.foundation: Exact Uint64/hex-token cells via a5-js cellToBoundary (segments auto) as derived geoarrow.wkb polygons with continuous longitudes beside the unchanged ID field; invalid cells keep source rows without footprints; resident polygon style, masks and picking; node tests cover bigint and hex spellings above 2^53
capabilities.gap: Rendered as derived polygon footprints through the resident GeoJSON renderer (Float32 coordinates), not browser-verified. Native s2/a5/geohash layers have no hierarchy or parent/child operations (checked in LAYERS4), so none are planned; fill/stroke/size/height channels, 3D and wireframe depend on the shared polygon path and need qualification.
capabilities.acceptance: Cell shape, level, styling and identity pass native fixtures in the pinned browser.

capabilities.title: Geohash
capabilities.foundation: Strings decoded once at publication (quotes stripped, case folded, 1-12 base32 characters) into exact bounds footprints as derived geoarrow.wkb polygons; mixed precision, nullable and invalid rows keep source identity; resident polygon style, masks and picking; node tests cover mixed precision
capabilities.gap: Rendered as derived polygon footprints through the resident GeoJSON renderer (Float32 coordinates), not browser-verified. Native s2/a5/geohash layers have no hierarchy or parent/child operations (checked in LAYERS4), so none are planned; fill/stroke/size/height channels, 3D and wireframe depend on the shared polygon path and need qualification.
capabilities.acceptance: Mixed precision geohashes retain correct bounds and source identity in the pinned browser.

capabilities.title: Flow map
capabilities.foundation: FlowmapGPULayer (flowmap-gpu-layer.ts): the native @flowmap.gl data provider (zoom-adaptive clustering, color scale, fade, adaptive scales, top-N) fed by GPU-resident aggregation (no row cap): float32-keyed location dedupe with native first-seen ids and masked origin-destination aggregation by GPU sort and segmented sum; only unique locations (max 262,144) and aggregated pairs (max 4,194,304) are read back. Rendering is WGSL ports of the flowmap.gl flow-line (arrowed, outlined, straight/curved/animated) and flow-circle shaders (GPUFlowLinesLayer, GPUFlowCirclesLayer) with flow and location picking, hover highlight and native Kepler tooltip objects. Bound visConfig: darkBaseMapEnabled, colorRange, opacity, flowFadeEnabled/Amount, flowLocationTotalsEnabled, flowLinesRenderingMode (straight, curved, animated-straight), flowLineThicknessScale, flowLineCurviness, flowClusteringEnabled, maxTopFlowsDisplayNum, flowAdaptiveScalesEnabled. Differences: float32 location identity and one aggregated datum per OD pair; positions are float32 on the GPU (no 64-bit low part). Optional flowmap.gl location labels (visConfig.flowLocationLabelsEnabled, styled from the first textLabel entry) drawn through the point-label GPU text path (flow-location-labels.ts: in-view locations, largest circles first, at most 1,024) and scale lock (visConfig.flowScaleLockEnabled freezes the flow and location-total domains). Kepler filters, including time filters, drive the GPU aggregation through the layer mask and totals are re-aggregated per revision (node-spec covered).
capabilities.gap: Browser-checked only by scripts/flow-h3.mjs and flow-h3-picking.mjs (both pass locally at ?rows=256: no WGSL validation errors, endpoint/cluster picking). Visual correctness of arrowheads, curves, animation and fade is NOT checked (backlog FLOW-3). Location labels (visConfig.flowLocationLabelsEnabled) now skip labels that overlap a larger circle's label (the bounded greedy placement used for point labels; label rectangles are estimated at 0.6 em per character, so they are approximate, and the set is recomputed when data or viewport refresh, not on every frame), and the Kepler layer panel gets two host switches (Location labels, Lock scales) plus a scale-lock status line showing the frozen flow and location-total domains (native-flow-config-controls.tsx, injected by wrapping LayerConfiguratorFactory); there is no map-corner scale-lock legend. Labels, collision, scale lock and the panel switches are node-spec covered and exercised by scripts/flow-labels.mjs (exit 0 on 2026-10-31 after one dev-server load timeout). No flowmap.gl-native time axis (Kepler time filters work through the layer mask), no GPU filter range (native FlowmapLayer also ignores GPU filters; resident row mask feeds the aggregation instead). Hover tooltip resolves asynchronously (like native, the object appears on the next hover event). Large-table memory unmeasured. H3 endpoint mode uses cell centers via the same aggregation (scripts/flow-h3.mjs, scripts/flow-h3-picking.mjs).
capabilities.acceptance: Selected links and node totals agree with explicit source and target aggregates.

capabilities.title: Flow field
capabilities.foundation: Resident class over the native Flow Field layer: u/v, speed+direction-from and downhill-altitude modes are binned into a bounded velocity grid on the GPU (flow-field-gpu.ts: mask-aware bin, mean, gradient, box smoothing, max-speed reduction, int32 fixed-point accumulation) driven directly by the layer selection mask, so filters (including time filters) re-bin with no mask or grid readback; the result is copied into the texture FlowParticleSimulation samples. The CPU grid remains as fallback (non-WebGPU, gridMode 'cpu', or GPU setup failure). luma FlowParticleSimulation integrates on the GPU (midpoint, spherical m/s, seeded respawn, lifetime) and FlowParticleLayer draws streaks with no particle readback. Layer removal releases the runtime and GPU grids. Particle layer skips viewports that do not intersect the field.
capabilities.gap: Implemented in round 6 (scripts/flow-field-gpu.mjs, flow-field-style.mjs and flow-field-centroid-debug.mjs exit 0 on 2026-10-31; visual parity with Kepler not checked): color by speed (particles take one of up to eight equal speed bands from the layer colorRange via the grid cell under them; speed is normalized into the velocity texel w channel), viewport-concentrated spawning, terrain Z (bilinear altitude grid times elevationMultiplier, from the ELEVATION altitude or the optional altitude column), GeoJSON-column centroid positions (vertex average, first 500,000 rows), the debug grid overlay, and a grid extent that follows the filtered rows on the GPU path (atomic min/max reduction; only its 20-byte result is read back per filter revision). Nothing in the GPU grid path, color by speed, viewport spawning, terrain Z or the debug grid has run in a browser (backlog FLOW2-FF-1..4, FLOW3-3..FLOW3-5, FLOW3-D-1..3); only node specs (grid reference, runtime state machine, static shader binding checks) and a WebGL FlowParticleSimulation spawn-region spec ran. Differences from native: fixed-point sums add small quantization error; filtered bounds change the texture mapping (cells become non-square), re-seed the particles once per filter revision and cost one 20-byte readback; color by speed uses at most eight equal speed bands per particle position rather than per-line start speed; viewport spawning is a spawn rectangle (padded 10%), so particles outside it respawn immediately and pitched or globe views use the viewport bounding box; terrain Z smooths the altitude grid only over cells that have an altitude and, like the particle layer, is not depth-composited against 3D layers beyond the layer's normal depth test; GeoJSON centroids read the first 500,000 rows on the CPU and reuse a per-layer cache; the debug grid reads the grid back (debug only) and its overlay uses depthTest false without map-state blending parameters. The CPU grid remains the non-WebGPU fallback.
capabilities.acceptance: Seeded particles obey field units, time and lifecycle policies.

capabilities.title: Vector tiles
capabilities.foundation: Kepler tile fetch/decode and Deck rendering; host-side pure modules vector-tile-working-set.ts (bounded LRU decoded-tile admission with cpu memory reservations), vector-tile-feature-ids.ts (tile-independent feature ids and split-feature registry), vector-tile-analysis-scope.ts (viewport working set vs complete dataset decision API) and vector-tile-decoded-batch.ts (columnar batches and CPU filter mask planning); node specs only.
capabilities.gap: vector-tile-resident-{style,tile,layers}.ts now draw admitted tiles with GPU point/path/polygon layers fed by the resident GeometryRuntime binding (prepareGeometrySource + makeGeometryGPUVectors), a WGSL kernel computes the per-feature filter mask and fill color on the GPU, and the gathered mask is consumed by every draw; the controller suppresses Deck's MVT sublayers via renderSubLayers for wrapped layers. Style is translated by createNativeStylePlan (linear/sqrt/log/quantile/threshold; categorical unsupported). Limits: draw layers mirror the resident GeoJSON adapter's GPU layers rather than createResidentLayerClasses (needs a table-backed Kepler layer); style is not auto-derived from the live Kepler layer (setStyleFromNativeLayer/test hook only); only fill color is data-driven, width/radius/stroke are constant; picking/hover on tiles is disabled; filters are applied via the controller API/test hook not Kepler's filter UI; up to 4 filters, 16 palette stops; tile property columns are fixed at load time; Deck's TileLayer cache stays unbudgeted; property-hash ids can collide. Nothing has been run in a browser; only tsc and biome passed.
capabilities.acceptance: Pan/evict/reload preserves identity; incomplete populations cannot imply global inference.

capabilities.title: Raster tiles
capabilities.foundation: Kepler raster source; GPURaster and raster contributors; host NumericRasterSource ingestion (raster-tile-ingest.ts), GeoTIFF reader, EPSG:4326/3857 reprojection plan, CPU identify/zonal/band math reference and budgeted LRU band residency (node spec only, not browser-verified)
capabilities.gap: TILES3-2 (all unrun, node specs only): a WGSL RasterWgslLayer (raster-wgsl-layer.ts/-shader.ts/-wrap.ts) replaces Kepler's GLSL RasterLayer tile sublayers via a TileLayer renderSubLayers wrap, drawing r32float band textures (resident from the budgeted residency, else private uploads) with nodata/validity masking, band math presets b1..b4, value filter, colormap and RGB composite; identify adds a GPU texel readback row; zonal runs through GPURasterZonalStatistics per tile (zones rasterized on the CPU by pixel center, overlap falls back to CPU) with a React zonal panel; the GeoTIFF reader (raster-geotiff-cog.ts) handles tiled/strip, DEFLATE/LZW/PackBits, predictors 2/3, overviews and HTTP range reads. Limits: nothing has run in a browser or on a device (texture bindings with explicit group 3 layout, unfilterable-float sampling and draw order are unverified); terrain mesh sublayers, more than 4 source bands and unknown presets keep Kepler's draw (GLSL, no WebGPU); SWEEP-3 ported Kepler's linear rescale (value*scaler+offset), non-linear rescale with gamma, sigmoidal contrast and saturation, categorical colormap stepping (nearest, integer dtypes) and native single-band colormap placement (0.5*value+0.5, linear sampling, alpha = layer opacity) to WGSL (node specs for the plan and WGSL parse only; pixel parity vs Kepler's GLSL is not browser-verified); filter now compares the rescaled value like Kepler; index combinations without a colormap still draw gray instead of Kepler's red channel; saturation in single mode reads identity-filled bands 1 and 2; GPU zonal sums are float32 per tile and zones come from CPU rasterization (GPUPolygonRasterization not used); GPU identify is an extra tooltip row (async, cached) beside the CPU result; only EPSG:4326/3857 north-up; the sync GeoTIFF reader used by bitmap/analysis attach (raster-geotiff-reader.ts) now decodes COGs (classic/Big TIFF, tiled or strip, DEFLATE/LZW/PackBits, predictors 2/3) at full resolution, ignoring overviews (node spec only).
capabilities.acceptance: Band math and bounded identify agree across tile edges, nodata and eviction.

capabilities.title: WMS
capabilities.foundation: Pinned Kepler WMS source (one viewport image via deck BitmapLayer, EPSG:4326 in globe and EPSG:3857 otherwise); host-side wms-identify.ts provides pure GetMap/GetFeatureInfo URL building with 1.3.0 lat,lon axis order, TIME and I/J vs X/Y handling, time extent parsing, exception classification, attribution resolution and GeoJSON/GML/text identify parsing; node specs only.
capabilities.gap: TILES2-2 wired TIME injection and robust GetFeatureInfo into Kepler's native popover via prototype patches (wms-live-controller.ts); TILES3-2 added a React WMS time picker (wms-time-picker.tsx, wms-time-extent.ts) with capabilities Dimension/Extent parsing, ISO-8601 period expansion, slider/prev/next and typed TIME, mounted through RasterToolsPanel. Kepler's WMS image is a deck BitmapLayer, which ships a WGSL shader in deck 9.4, so no separate bitmap draw path was added; that draw is still unverified on WebGPU. Limits: scripts/wms.mjs exit 0 on 2026-10-31 (headless; scope is what that script asserts); the picker reads GetCapabilities from layer.meta.tilesetDataUrl and visConfig.wmsLayer.name (shape unverified); time dimension handling ignores current/nearest-value semantics; analysis still requires a numeric source.
capabilities.acceptance: CRS, axis order, time, capabilities errors and attribution behave correctly.

capabilities.title: 3D tiles
capabilities.foundation: Pinned Kepler 3D tile loader and renderer; Deck Tile3DLayer sublayers use WGSL (no vs:/fs: injection in tile-3d-layer)
capabilities.gap: Picking: src/tile3d-picking.ts clones Kepler's Tile3D layer with pickable:true so picking works outside annotation mode (wired in main.tsx layer pipeline; verified 2026-10-31: scripts/tile3d-effects.mjs exit 0, pick returns a hit). The synthetic tileset route in scripts/tile3d-effects.mjs handles CORS preflight/HEAD and uses 3D Tiles 1.0 asset version. Runtime checks (verified 2026-10-31, tile3d-effects.mjs exit 0): scripts/tile3d-effects.mjs serves a synthetic one-tile glb tileset and, through the test hook (getTile3DDiagnostics, pickTile3D, getDeviceResourceCounts), asserts tile model matrices, picking and that GPU resources drop after layer removal. Kepler enables Tile3D picking only in annotation mode, so feature picking hits and selected features are not exercised by default; load errors (Kepler logs to console) and eviction under memory pressure are not verified. EFFECTS2: 3D tile scenegraphs now cast and receive WGSL shadow maps and use Kepler's simple-phong override while Light and Shadow has shadow lights (installScenegraphShadowPatch; GPU spec on a synthetic glTF only, not against a real tileset).
capabilities.acceptance: Tile transforms, feature picking, load errors and eviction pass.

capabilities.title: Bitmap overlay
capabilities.foundation: Pinned Kepler bitmap bounds editor; bitmap-georeference.ts (bounds/corners/opacity mapping, world file, resource scope) and GeoTIFF numeric input via raster-geotiff-reader.ts
capabilities.gap: raster-live-bitmap.ts reads the live bitmap layer visConfig through the georeference resolver and can attach a GeoTIFF for numeric identify and bounds; TILES3-2 found that Kepler's bitmap layer draws with deck's BitmapLayer (WGSL-capable in deck 9.4) so no new draw path was written. Still open: no UI dispatches the bounds patch, the bitmap attach sync GeoTIFF reader now handles tiled/compressed COGs at full resolution (overviews ignored, 64 MB input cap; node spec only), nothing has run in a browser, bounds-editor round trip, image export and texture cleanup are not verified in the host; plain images never supply analysis values; rotated corners are mapped but not editable.
capabilities.acceptance: Edited bounds, opacity, image export and resource cleanup match the host.

capabilities.title: Import local and remote data
capabilities.foundation: Native Load Files datasets (CSV, GeoJSON, Arrow, saved maps) are prepared automatically under their original IDs with roles read from native layers, a visible Float32 rounding policy and keeping native layers/filters/tooltips; manual Prepare data, Arrow IPC and SQL result publication with explicit schema, precision and roles remain
capabilities.gap: Auto-prepare is unverified in a browser; arc/line layers from tabular endpoint columns have no published connection binding; one role set per dataset (additional layers using other columns warn); CPU materialization is capped at 1,000,000 rows / 16,000,000 cells; unsupported Arrow types are excluded with a reason; remote CSV/GeoJSON/Parquet/Arrow URLs and local CSV/GeoJSON/Parquet files decode on the CPU via remote-source-loader.ts (Open from URL, size cap, progress, cancel) but are unverified in a browser; CSV is all-text type inference (no time parsing), Parquet needs parquet-wasm codecs and undeclared hoisted deps (d3-dsv, parquet-wasm), no streaming or resume for these formats. BINDING3: restore of several sources rolls back the failing source's partial upload and lists every source that cannot be allocated; unqualified with a real allocation failure in a browser.
capabilities.acceptance: Import two unrelated datasets, filter independently and retain IDs, nulls and original values.

capabilities.title: Replace, append, delete and refresh
capabilities.foundation: Versioned registry, per-dataset consumers, native publication/removal and portable restoration under original dataset IDs
capabilities.gap: BINDING3: every dataset replacement path (automatic republish, evicted-table rebuild, restore source creation, recomputed results) and removal runs through the per-dataset DatasetOperationQueue, and restoreBundle waits for it to be idle; a failed restore now also releases the partial upload of the failing source and reports every source that cannot be allocated (binding3-restore-recovery.ts). BINDING4: allocation failures are now typed (KeplerAllocationError from the dataset registry budget/reservation paths, scalar/scope/session working-memory checks and several example runtimes; luma core OutOfMemoryError for device buffer and texture out-of-memory) and detected with isKeplerAllocationError, no message matching; BINDING5: the remaining budget, reservation and capacity throws (point labels, raster bands, aggregation, group-by, style, scopes, explorer/inspector readback budgets and the analysis catalog capacity checks) are now KeplerAllocationError with their old messages; export, bundle-payload and input-validation limits stay plain Errors. During restore each source attach runs inside a WebGPU out-of-memory error scope (binding5-device-oom-scope.ts) so a device out-of-memory becomes a thrown allocation error and rolls back; the scope is device-wide and unverified against a real OOM. Readback races and the whole path are node-spec covered only; no browser or injected-OOM qualification yet.
capabilities.acceptance: Replace/delete during readback cannot publish stale results or destroy borrowed resources.

capabilities.title: Precision, nulls and time types
capabilities.foundation: Schema/Float64 precision preview, dictionary labels, exact signed 64-bit timestamps, bounded original-value native table and lossless original Arrow exports including geometry; source-type-routes.ts routes Int64/Uint64/Decimal (exact decimal category or opt-in Float64), Float16, Time, Duration, LargeUtf8, WKT/WKB (derived GeoJSON), nested/Binary/Interval/Null (retained JSON/hex text, excluded with reason) with visible per-field routes
capabilities.gap: Exact GPU wide integer primitives exist (wide-numeric-gpu-*.ts: Int64/Uint64 add, subtract, compare, multiply to 64 and 128 bits, divide by a small divisor, exact 128-bit sums, min, max, count, Float32 conversion with an exactness flag, exact range predicates) and are GPU-spec tested against BigInt. DATA4 wired them into (a) SQL: SELECT COUNT/SUM/MIN/MAX(col or *) [AS alias] FROM t [WHERE col op integer AND ...] over an Int64/Uint64 column runs on the exact kernels (results beyond Int32 are published as exact decimal text because the resident store narrows 64-bit columns to Float32; GROUP BY, AVG, OR and mixed predicates keep their normal route), and (b) Big Number charts on whole-population Int64/Uint64 sum, mean, min and max (exact-value note in the chart). A Decimal128 kernel now exists (exact sum, min, max, count, null count and compare against a decimal constant of any scale, four-word values, BigInt reference, GPU spec), but it is NOT wired into SQL, charts or filters (Arrow Decimal columns still hit the precision-policy rejection in the resident store) and its compare feeds counts, not a Kepler filter mask. Still not exact: grouped, time and plot chart measures over 64-bit columns, selected-population charts, median and standard deviation, numeric filter UI for 64-bit columns, exact sums are only guaranteed below 2^32 rows, and the 128-bit multiply is unsigned only. All of this is node and headless-GPU spec verified only (backlog DATA4-W1, DATA4-W2), no browser run. Type routes are node-tested but unverified in a browser; Time/Duration become Float64 seconds subject to the Float32 policy. Prepared GPU measurements remain distinct from exact original values; bounded nested/text previews may truncate, while original Arrow export retains them.
capabilities.acceptance: Sliced nullable data, large IDs, Float64, dictionary changes and pre-1970 timestamps pass.

capabilities.title: Group by and aggregate
capabilities.foundation: Native panel wiring and bounded all-row dictionary grouping; count and Float32 sum/average/min/max; dedicated result adoption, native schema and snapshot lineage
capabilities.gap: The GPU runtime now executes the planner: planKeplerGroupByPasses splits a Group By into key windows (addKeplerGroupBy keyWindow over dictionary slots, one per-graph pass up to 1,048,576 slots, fewer when the 256 MiB working budget requires) crossed with batches of 16 measures, each pass reads back only its group prefix, and mergeKeplerGroupByPasses restores first-occurrence order (merged result uploaded as new GPU buffers); caps are now 128 measures, 4,194,304 dictionary slots, 67,108,864 source rows (memory reservation governs), 32 MiB key text and 256 MiB result. Multi-pass merge is CPU-side over the bounded result rows; the dictionary code is the perfect hash, so there is no separate GPU hash table. Single-pass kernel change (keyWindow) and multi-pass path are typecheck and node-spec only (merge model and planner run); GPU and browser qualification pending. No median/std/count-distinct on GPU (CPU references only in analysis-group-by-extended.ts). Unordered string dictionary key only; other configurations require explicit SQL. SQL4: the SQL GROUP BY path (LuSQL dense group aggregation) now removes empty dictionary slots by adding or reusing a COUNT(*) presence column and compacting the live groups on the GPU; it passed a headless WebGPU spec (string-key groups with WHERE LIKE, SUM over CAST(x AS DOUBLE)); LuSQL GROUP BY still has one key and count/sum/min/max/mean over float32 columns only (use CAST(col AS DOUBLE) for integers). SQL5: GROUP BY over string-function results, CAST(numeric AS VARCHAR) and join output works through the same dictionary presence column (headless specs resident-sql-expressions-gpu.spec.ts and resident-sql-compose-gpu.spec.ts); still one key per statement. SQL6: GROUP BY keys may be string expressions over three to eight dictionary columns (bounded mixed-radix lookup) and CAST(numeric AS VARCHAR) with up to 1,048,576 distinct values (was 65,536); the SQL path still has one GROUP BY key per statement, aggregates over float32 only, and no median/std/count-distinct on the GPU.
capabilities.acceptance: Null keys, first-occurrence order, count of all rows, null-only groups, bounded result readback, no reupload, cancellation and standalone saved-result recovery match native semantics and declared Float32 policy.

capabilities.title: Attribute joins
capabilities.foundation: GPU key canonicalization, stable sort, duplicate-aware range probe and scans; only a 16-byte summary is read back before output allocation and payload columns are gathered on the GPU. No input or output row cap (uint32 row indices, memory reservation and device limits apply); publication is size-gated: results of at most 262,144 rows are read back, validated (validity 0 or 1, dictionary code range) and adopted with adoptArrowDataset (full cells, device recovery, DuckDB, export and labels); larger results stay GPU-resident via adoptResidentDataset with no result readback (rows page in lazily for tooltips and table views; over-cap results have no CPU source, so device recovery and eviction rebuild recompute them from recorded lineage (operation, inputs, parameters) under the same dataset ID, and they show null cells only where rows are not paged in (the native data table and tooltips page them); source export, analysis export and the portable sandbox bundle stream the needed rows from GPU pages into the accounted lazy view, DuckDB registration does the same for resident sources, and point labels are limited to 100,000 rows)
capabilities.gap: SQL joins now carry right-side columns: INNER, LEFT, RIGHT (as a swapped LEFT) and FULL joins with right columns in SQL select order run on the resident join executor (GPU key canonicalization, duplicate-aware range probe, output-parallel fill, GPU gathers of left and right columns) and duplicateRightMatches all/first/last is honoured (headless WebGPU spec modules/kepler/test/resident-sql-strings-gpu.spec.ts checks all three policies for INNER and LEFT, plus FULL and RIGHT, against nested-loop SQL semantics). Policies now drive execution: duplicateRightMatches (all, first, last) changes the GPU probe pass (oracle and step-for-step GPU mirror agree in node spec; the GPU probe pass for all/first/last now also runs in the SQL join spec), rightColumnSuffix and dropRightKey name colliding right columns by suffix instead of the native label prefix in the plan (pure, tested), and both persist in the join lineage. Null keys never match and key precision stays exact by construction (dictionary strings and integral Float32; 64-bit refusal in the planner). A host companion panel (analysis4-join-policy-panel.tsx, Join policies) edits the three options on the pending native join operation via setJoinConfig, so the native Run button executes them (node spec of the record listing only; browser verification pending). The native Join panel itself is unchanged. Browser verification of the native Join panel and the policy panel is still pending; SQL5: SQL joins now compose with WHERE, GROUP BY, ORDER BY, LIMIT and expressions (resident intermediate then the normal SQL stages), accept up to 4 ON equalities (exact mixed radix for string keys; ) and SEMI/ANTI joins (left columns only), verified by headless WebGPU spec resident-sql-compose-gpu.spec.ts (4 tests); also fixed integer-key SQL joins that failed bind-group creation. Remaining: joins of more than two tables, subqueries, CROSS JOIN, non-equality ON, and browser verification (fixture ?sqlFixture=strings, backlog SQL5-F-2). SQL6: numeric multi-column keys are now exact for every join type and duplicate policy: before the executor runs, a GPU distinct pass ranks each numeric key column across both sides (resident-join-composite-rank.ts), the ranks fold into the same mixed radix as string keys, and the existing probe emits matches and unmatched rows (headless spec resident-sql-compose-gpu.spec.ts checks LEFT, RIGHT, FULL, SEMI, ANTI and a mixed string/integer key against nested-loop semantics; node oracle covers sint32 and float32). The hashed key with exact residual survives only as the INNER-with-all-matches fallback when the radix product exceeds 32 bits or a key column has more than 1,048,576 distinct values; other types and policies then retry on DuckDB with the reason. Joins whose result or a side has no rows are refused at execution and retried on DuckDB. ANTI JOIN can select right columns (always NULL); SEMI JOIN cannot, as in DuckDB. Browser verification still pending (fixture queries join-numeric-multi-key-left, semi/anti-join-numeric-multi-key were added but self-joins of one resident table are untested).
capabilities.acceptance: One-to-many joins either execute correctly or route explicitly; result IDs are stable.

capabilities.title: Spatial joins
capabilities.foundation: GPU point-in-polygon with spatial index and resident aggregates; no point/polygon/pair cap; chunks of 1,048,576 points on one prepared polygon index with fused GPU aggregation, 256 MiB join working memory per chunk, compensated Float32 sums, and size-gated publication: results of at most 262,144 rows are read back, validated (validity 0 or 1, dictionary code range, non-finite aggregates refused) and adopted with adoptArrowDataset (full cells, device recovery, exports); larger results stay GPU-resident with no result readback, a four byte GPU flag that still refuses non-finite aggregates, and lazily paged rows (over-cap: recomputed from lineage after device loss or eviction, null cells only where rows are not paged in, DuckDB, export, labels and sandbox bundle refused); Merge of the polygon geometry column (the native panel default) is a bounded CPU step with accounted readback of at most 4,194,304 matched pairs, native mergeGeometries semantics and GeoJSON Feature string cells, limited to results of at most 262,144 rows and refused above that with an uncheck-merge message
capabilities.gap: CRS: the host panel 'Spatial join CRS' (analysis4-spatial-join-crs-panel.tsx, beside the native Spatial Join panel) sets the point-side and polygon-side CRS on the pending join operation as a preset (EPSG:4326, EPSG:3857) or any supported EPSG code or proj4 parameter string. Supported: EPSG:4326/3857 and aliases, UTM EPSG codes (326NN, 327NN, 258NN ETRS89, 269NN NAD83) and proj4 +proj=longlat, utm and tmerc (any central meridian, scale, false origin, latitude origin) on a WGS84/GRS80-class ellipsoid or explicit +a/+rf, plus spherical +proj=merc. Same-CRS joins run directly (planar test); different CRSs move the points into the polygon CRS with a GPU pass (resident-spatial-join-reproject.ts) that unprojects the point CRS to longitude/latitude and projects into the polygon CRS, using the Krueger series (the same series as proj4's etmerc) in Float32 (resident-spatial-join-crs.ts). The CPU reference matches proj4 2.22 within 5 mm (node spec) and the GPU kernel matches proj4 on the Float32 inputs within 3 to 6 m across 4326, 3857, UTM north and south and a national-style tmerc (headless GPU spec), the error being Float32 and growing with northing; a full GPU join with a projected side, and the panel, are not browser-run. Refused, not guessed: other projections (Lambert, Albers, stereographic ...), datum shifts (+towgs84 with non-zero terms, nadgrids), non-metre units, prime meridians and axis orders; polygons are never reprojected (a 4326 polygon column joined with UTM points moves the points into 4326), resident sources carry no CRS metadata so the user must declare it, and a point side stored as longitude/latitude roles that really hold projected coordinates is trusted as declared. The GPU path still uses its own predicate kernels; the reference predicate semantics in analysis-join-policy.ts are an oracle, not the executor. GPU/browser verification pending.
capabilities.acceptance: Boundary points, holes, null geometry and many-to-many output pass.

capabilities.title: Suitability analysis
capabilities.foundation: Native RUN_SUITABILITY on a resident source runs a GPUCompositeScore executor: GPU weighted overlay of up to 16 resident columns with per-column GPU statistics; no CPU row cap (kernel limit 16,777,216 rows). Columns are scored with min-max or z-score standardization and a weighted sum (normalized or raw weights), per-column statistics refuse constant columns, and the score is published size-gated (at most 262,144 rows: read back, validated and adopted with adoptArrowDataset, device-recoverable and exportable; larger results GPU-resident with no result readback, lazily paged rows, recomputed from lineage after device loss or eviction, and DuckDB, export, labels and sandbox bundle refused) with the carried columns as a separate table-only result with native schema (carried fields then a real score field, unique naming), derivedDataset lineage and portable-bundle persistence. A row missing any weighted value scores null, as native
capabilities.gap: Raw data standardization is accepted (weighted raw values; GPU standardization pass skipped, constant columns allowed); node spec compares it with the native oracle, GPU unrun. GPU and native workflow qualification pending (implemented ahead of verification). Float32 policy: weighted values and scores are Float32 and integers beyond +/-16,777,216 are refused. Weights above 1 are divided by the largest weight with a visible workflow note, up to 128 weighted fields, and categorical string-dictionary fields are reclassified on the GPU through a per-code lookup: dictionary position by default, or caller category scores that the host policy panel now collects (a textarea per operation, one field per line as field: label=score, parsed and refused when a score is not finite; passed to the run request and its key; node-tested, browser typing unverified; Kepler native panel still has no category score control and labels missing from the scores score null). Still rejected exactly rather than approximated: negative or all-zero weights, other non-numeric fields, and constant weighted columns (native leaves them unstandardized). Missing-value policy for weighted fields missing in only some rows is user-chosen in the host panel (refuse, exclude as native, or renormalize as a non-native extension recorded in lineage). Per-column standardization statistics are over each column's own defined values in all policies. One resident source; at most 16,777,216 rows (kernel limit), 32 output columns, result bounded by memory reservation; carried columns are Float32, Int32, Uint32 or dictionary strings; empty inputs refused. The native operation has no constraints or rasters, so none are claimed.
capabilities.acceptance: Range and z-score scores, normalized and raw weights, null scores for missing values, output naming and lineage reproduce the pinned native result within the declared Float32 policy; unsupported shapes show explicit guidance and stale or cancelled runs publish nothing.

capabilities.title: Time, intervals and playback
capabilities.foundation: Native exact timestamp range filters, minute-of-day controls and GPU time-window selection; bounded native time histograms with compiled interval edges, nullable epoch bins, self-filter exclusion and saved interval replay
capabilities.gap: DATA4 wiring (node specs and headless GPU specs pass; no browser run yet, backlog DATA4-1..): (1) The time-contract interval WGSL is now compiled and run on a GPU against the BigInt oracle for all 16 closure combinations, null starts, open-ended rows, chunked words and four windows (time-contract-interval-gpu.ts, time-contract-interval-gpu.spec.ts), and drives TimeRuntime when a dataset declares an interval (declareTimeInterval(datasetId, startColumn, {endColumn, closure}) before publication; native filters carrying that endName are then accepted; the declaration is a programmatic host API with no UI). (2) Zone-aware bucketing: the host Time contract panel sets a zone (UTC, fixed offset or IANA); 1-day, 1-hour and 1-minute time histograms then use local wall-clock edges (23 and 25 hour days, repeated fall-back hours) built from the zone offset table, validated against Intl in a node spec for America/New_York and +05:30; other intervals stay UTC, and native Kepler itself buckets by UTC and uses a zone only for labels. Zone offsets are tabulated on the CPU at planning, not looked up in a kernel. (3) Exact playback: the panel's ExactPlaybackDriver steps the bigint playback machine from requestAnimationFrame timestamps and writes the native filter value through the same setFilterAnimationTime action Kepler's AnimationController dispatches (the native animation is paused first), so the native slider, histogram and resident masks follow it; modes free, incremental, point and snap-to-histogram-bins, overhang and loop. Node-spec tested with a fake host only; nothing compares its frames with Kepler's own controller in a browser, snap and speed/window changes mid-play are our own definitions, and the native time widget's own animation controls still exist beside it. (4) Source encodings (epoch s/ms/us/ns, ISO8601, date, time-of-day, duration) remain a node-tested parser that ingestion does not call. Time histograms: up to 16,384 intervals (GPU spec: 1,000 exact bins); above 512 bars non-grouped vertical bar charts render on a canvas (resident-chart-bars-canvas.tsx, per-pixel-column decimation, hover tooltip, click and drag-brush selection); the layout is node-tested (16,384 bars across 800 px) and time-histogram-canvas.mjs is written, but neither canvas versus SVG render time nor brush selection has been measured in a browser, and horizontal, line, grouped and grid charts still use SVG at any bin count. Remaining: DST edges not on whole minutes, zone coverage tested on a few zones, in-kernel zone lookup, a UI for interval columns, browser qualification of everything above.
capabilities.acceptance: Four focused GPU cases pass exact signed and submillisecond edge classification, nulls, chunks, scopes and retirement. Nine native checks pass Month/Year controls, pinned edge/count oracles, self-exclusion, unrelated filters, visible SVG, replay and unchanged source buffers/uploads/batches.

capabilities.title: 3D view, split maps and swipe
capabilities.foundation: Default single-Deck Dual and Swipe: two viewports in one Deck on the shared WebGPU device, per-view layer visibility from native split maps, each half keeps its own maplibre basemap under the transparent shared canvas, and Swipe gives each view its side of the divider via a sub-rectangle projection so geography matches a full-size map. Each view has its own view state (synchronized or unlocked), pan/zoom, hover and click routed to its native map, point labels and elevated points per view, and the swipe percentage and split layers round-trip through native configuration and through exported portable bundles (Swipe, and Dual with unsynchronized viewports). Wheel zoom pivots exactly at the pointer in every view, pitched/rotated 3D slices exactly like the full-size map in Swipe, GlobeView renders one seamless globe in Swipe and one per view in Dual, one-finger pan and two-finger pinch work per view with touch emulation, and the native polygon draw tool and Select Geometry operate in either view. A maps layout keeps the Deck mounted across Single, Dual and Swipe, and closing either map keeps the Deck and device. `?views=1` restores the single-view host that rejects split and swipe.
capabilities.gap: Browser checks are headless WebGPU Chromium only. Select-by-click of an existing editor feature: the asynchronous editor supplies its own multi-pick hit as the click target when Deck's pointer-down pick is another layer (scripts/views-editor-select.mjs exit 0, verified 2026-10-31 for Single, Swipe and the left view of Dual); a DualRight case for the right-hand view and a deselect click there was added and has not been run. Selection is not qualified with unlocked (unsynchronized) view states, in Globe views or on touch. Globe wheel zoom uses an exact ray-sphere pivot whose browser verification is pending. Touch recognition thresholds vary by several pixels between gestures.
capabilities.acceptance: Two views have correct independent layer visibility; closing one does not destroy the other.

capabilities.title: Globe projection
capabilities.foundation: Deck GlobeView in the pinned host on WebGPU: Kepler GLSL atmosphere/halo layers are omitted, WebGL parameters are translated, the view clear flags removed and the GLSL depth disk is replaced by the WGSL GPUGlobeDepthDiskLayer (far-side basemap tiles are depth-occluded). Resident points, lines, arcs (with great-circle arrowheads), mesh icons, point labels, GeoJSON polygons/outlines/extrusion/paths/points, H3 (polygon branch), Trips, heatmaps (native data-bounds density frame on a WGSL tessellated sphere mesh) and grid/hexagon/cluster aggregates draw, cull at the horizon and pick where native picks (scripts/globe.mjs, gpu-globe.spec.ts). GeoJSON long edges follow Deck's globe preparation: a globe variant of the prepared geometry (antimeridian unwrap, 5-degree linear edge subdivision, 5-degree polygon grid cuts) is derived once per published source from the retained source and accounted in the memory registry.; the globe variant is now prepared in time slices for GeoJSON-row sources (other encodings in one deferred step), planar geometry draws until it is ready, it is rebuilt per zoom band (5/2/1 degrees with hysteresis, one resident variant, registry-reserved, over-budget bands fall back) and released on leaving globe (globe-geometry-variants.ts, scripts/globe-rebuild.mjs not yet run)
capabilities.gap: First globe frames show planar geometry until the variant is ready; non-GeoJSON encodings still decode in one uninterrupted step and the slices run on the main thread (no worker). SHARING3: once the globe variant is ready the planar GeometryRuntime (GPU vectors, gathers, GPU reservation) is released after a 1.5 s grace (planar-geometry-hibernation.ts) and rebuilt in time slices on exit while the globe variant keeps drawing; bounds, invalid-row count, feature types and the retained polygon analysis source are cached, representative points for polygon filters come from the globe variant meanwhile (antimeridian-unwrapped, so filters on antimeridian-crossing polygons may differ), and a failed rebuild keeps the globe variant with a notice. A failed finer-band swap while released forces a planar rebuild with a short gap. Dual/Swipe choose the band from the primary map zoom only. None of this is browser-verified (scripts/globe-planar-release.mjs exit 0, verified 2026-10-31). Finer bands exceed native Kepler's fixed 5 degrees and are unverified for pixel parity. Arc and icon globe scenarios already exist in globe.mjs (icon-wide stays unqualified); no new arc/icon work was needed. Aggregate cells are inverse-projected from Web Mercator common space in float32. Cluster centers follow the planar viewport bounds, which is also what pinned native Kepler's cluster query does (getViewportBounds at the rounded zoom), so no globe-specific bounds were added. Heatmaps use the native data-bounds density frame on a tessellated sphere mesh (resident-globe-heatmap-layer.ts) and are checked only for drawing and horizon culling, not pixel parity with native. Grid, hexagon and heatmap inside Swipe and Dual globes now have a browser script (scripts/globe-split-aggregates.mjs exit 0, per-side draw and per-map layer visibility, verified 2026-10-31). GPUMeshColumnLayer has no globe or horizon branch, but it is only used for the H3 columns branch and a globe viewport selects the H3 polygon branch (the same rule as native Kepler), so extruded H3 and GeoJSON cells on a globe draw through GPUSolidPolygonLayer extrusion (globe.mjs extrusion and h3-extruded scenarios) and a true mesh-column globe path does not exist; 3D mesh icons (GPUMeshIconLayer) are covered by the icon scenarios. Atmosphere/halo layers are omitted. EFFECTS3: globe viewports now draw WGSL shadow maps with a sphere-fitted orthographic light projection (not browser-verified in the app; coarse resolution).
capabilities.acceptance: Globe drawing and picking match native Kepler for each remaining layer before it is enabled.

capabilities.gap: EFFECTS2: real WGSL shadow mapping now exists (deck-gpu-layers wgsl-shadow.ts, wgsl-shadow-effect.ts: light-space RGBA8 packed-depth pass over participating layers with Deck's light matrices, shadowColor, time-of-day SunLight direction refreshed per viewport, night-time uniform shadow, 2 lights, bilinear PCF lookup). It is verified by GPU specs for column layers and glTF scenegraphs but NOT yet in the full Kepler app (scripts/effects-shadow-map.mjs failed once for an unrelated wall-pipeline limit, fixed in EFFECTS3-R1, effects-shadow-map.mjs exit 0 on 2026-10-31). EFFECTS3: participating layers (cast and receive) now are GPUSolidPolygonLayer (fill, walls, wireframe: GeoJSON, H3/S2/A5/geohash extruded cells), GPUMeshColumnLayer, GPUColumnLayer (grid and hexagon cell cores, ArrowColumnLayer/ArrowGridCellLayer), GPUScatterplotLayer (points, billboard and meshes), GPUPathLayer (shadow pass draws the real ribbon even for billboard paths, unlike Deck's collapsed center line), GPUArcLayer, GPULineLayer, GPUPointCloudLayer, GPUIconLayer (receive only; icons are 2D), and every ScenegraphLayer (3D tiles, trip markers). Deck adds its shadow module to every layer as a default module and effective participation is decided by whether the layer shader calls the DECKGL_FILTER_GL_POSITION/COLOR hooks. EFFECTS4 audited node_modules/@deck.gl/*/dist: text (multi-icon + text background), bitmap, icon, scatterplot (Kepler ArrowHeadLayer extends it), SimpleMesh/Scenegraph call the hooks; the final HeatmapLayer triangle layer does NOT (only the offscreen weights pass does) and glow/sky/atmosphere have no native counterpart, so heatmaps and glow stay non-participating by design. EFFECTS4 added GPUPointLabelLayer (glyphs and backgrounds), GPUBitmapLayer, GPUArrowHeadLayer (cast+receive) and GPUMeshIconLayer (already shared GPUScatterplotLayer's shader; now covered by a spec). Still NOT participating: the generic GPUTextLayer host (its shaders come from @luma.gl/text strategies/caller modelProps, no shadow hooks yet, EFFECTS4-5), glow/sky/atmosphere, heatmaps (native parity) and the basemap; ground shadows only land on participating layers. Views: every viewport gets its own shadow map fitted to that viewport (split/dual maps, verified by a two-pane pixel spec); map views use Deck's ground-plane fitting, orbit/orthographic views fit the light frustum to scene bounds (explicit sceneBounds, else layers' getBounds, else the view frustum with far plane clamped to 2x camera distance) and globe views fit it to the visible sphere with Deck's SunLight global direction (spec: tower on a globe darkens the surface; EFFECTS4: globe viewports now use a light-space fit rotated to the smallest cap extent and a larger map under a budget (globeShadowMapSize default 2048, globeShadowTexelBudget default 2048x2048 per light, clamped to maxTextureDimension2D; getViewportShadowStats reports shadowMapSize/texelsPerMeter vs the old baseline; spec shows 8x texels per meter in a 256x128 test). This is a single fitted map, NOT cascades: a close-up globe view gets the same budget as a whole-globe view, texture aspect follows the viewport, cap extent is estimated from a 9x9 sample grid, and ~25 MB per light at the budget; all unqualified against Kepler in the app, EFFECTS4-4). Kepler's editor-layer exclusion is mirrored (ids starting kepler_editor_layer neither cast, receive nor are lit; pixel spec uses the same prefix mechanism). Limits: at most 2 shadow lights; shadow map is viewport sized with Deck's 16-bit depth and bias, so fine-detail quality and any visual difference from Kepler's WebGL shadows are unverified; in the full Kepler app only the single-map extruded-polygon scenario of scripts/effects-shadow-map.mjs ran (exit 0 on 2026-10-31, shadow pixel metric unchanged); the rest is GPU specs on synthetic scenes; pixel-size offsets of billboard points/lines/arcs are applied in light clip space like Deck, so their shadow footprint is only roughly scaled; EFFECTS4 audit: GPUColumnLayer, GPUArcLayer, GPUPointCloudLayer and GPUIconLayer now all return premultiplied alpha (Deck's WebGPU layer pass blends one/one-minus-src-alpha; picking and the shadow-depth pass bypass blending), verified for columns by a native-parity plus analytic spec of translucent columns over a basemap (gpu-column-translucent.spec.ts; layer opacity is gamma-corrected by Deck as opacity^(1/2.2)); arcs, point clouds and icons are covered only by regression specs, not a dedicated translucent spec (EFFECTS4-3). EFFECTS3-R1: the earlier EFFECTS2-3 failure was a vertex storage-buffer overflow in extruded polygon walls with fp64 lows on 'core' devices (fixed, spec added), not the shadow patch itself. The screen-space pass (effects-wgsl-shadow-pass.ts) remains the fallback with a visible reason (getEffectReplacements shadowSkipReason) only for scenes with no participating layer, WebGL, or a globe not in view. Fog passes only run while the effect is the first post-process effect that still has the scene depth attachment (same limit as Kepler); fog, lighting and eviction/device-loss release are not browser-verified (scripts/tile3d-effects.mjs, TILES2-3xx backlog). Saved settings are untouched because only rendering is replaced.

capabilities.title: Data table, sorting and statistics
capabilities.foundation: Native asynchronous prepared/original/derived table; exact Float64/Int64/timestamp values, bounded geometry/text previews, collision-safe names and cross-batch GPU scalar sorting; exact bounded asynchronous CPU sorting of original strings, dictionaries, dates, timestamps, Int64 and Float64 (at most 262,144 rows, stable, missing last); native Kepler column statistics and exact column copy over the bounded population; pinned columns; keyboard preview wrapping
capabilities.gap: Float32 statistics reduce on the GPU (fused column profile, up to 16,777,216 rows; exact moments, null count and histogram, interior quantiles estimated from the histogram, distinct estimate) and Float32/Int32/Uint32 columns sort on the GPU at any row count (Int32/Uint32 assumed exact in the prepared scalar, unverified); dictionary strings, Int64/Uint64/timestamp/Date64/Time64 and Float64 sort on the GPU above 262,144 rows (strings: dictionary codes remapped through a sorted-dictionary rank table; 64-bit and Float64: two stable GPU passes over order-preserving hi/lo words, NaN and missing last; resident-table-gpu-sorter.ts) while at most 262,144 rows still use the exact bounded CPU sort. The 64-bit/Float64 GPU sort needs the retained Arrow words, which GPU-only resident datasets do not keep (refused with a stated reason), the words are transformed on the CPU while uploading, working memory is about 36 bytes per row (512 MiB admission), descending tie order relies on the stable global sort, and nothing was run on a GPU. Statistics for those types still run on the bounded CPU path (at most 262,144 rows, refused above). Column operations: display format is dispatched to Kepler (setColumnDisplayFormat); delete removes dependent filters and the tooltip field through Kepler actions and is refused while a layer uses the column, and deleted columns and rename aliases are applied by getResidentExportColumns (not yet wired into the export dialogs); rename is a table/export alias only (layers, filters, tooltips and GPU buffers keep the source name because the Kepler field is not renamed), the type change converts cells for display only (statistics and sort keep the source type), and create filter needs a dataset field (not a computed analysis column). Binary, list and struct fields have no order; large cells remain bounded previews with complete values in original Arrow export. Unverified in a browser. NATIVEUI4: Rename and type change dispatch Kepler renameTableColumn/changeTableColumnType (layers, filters, tooltips and channels follow natively) and re-prepare the resident dataset through NativeAutoPrepare.requestRepublish when the Kepler dataset is Arrow-backed and within automatic-preparation limits; otherwise they fall back to the display alias with the reason shown. Aliases and deleted columns are applied to bounded and streaming resident exports (CSV and Arrow). The table follows the GPU brush for every resident point dataset (brush mask ANDed into nativeFilteredMask while active). The republish path and brush link are unverified in a browser. SWEEP-2: Delete column dispatches Kepler deleteTableColumn (dependent filters, tooltip fields and channels dropped natively; still refused while a layer uses the column) and republishes under the same id when the dataset is Arrow-backed; otherwise it falls back to hide-from-view with the reason shown. Spec only; republish unverified in a browser. NATIVEUI6: Statistics for dictionary strings (GPU profile of the prepared codes: null count and an HLL distinct estimate), Int64/Uint64/timestamp/Date64 and Float64 (a Float32 copy relative to the column minimum built in one CPU conversion pass, then reduced by the fused GPU profile) now run above 262,144 rows up to 16,777,216 (resident-table-wide-statistics.ts); values are Float32-rounded relative to the range, quantiles are histogram estimates, string statistics give no per-value counts, and GPU-only resident datasets (no retained Arrow values) still refuse 64-bit/Float64 statistics with the reason. For GPU-only datasets the 64-bit/Float64 table sort now uses the prepared Float32 column when one exists (approximate: values round to Float32, not the exact two-pass hi/lo sort). Create filter from a computed analysis column stays unsupported: Kepler filters need a dataset field. Node specs only; no GPU or browser run.
capabilities.acceptance: Next page, sort and selected count agree without downloading all selected indices.

Grouped summaries cap series cross-products at 4,096 cells including a missing-label slot; chart cards measure Float32, Int32 and Uint32 fields (integers are widened on the GPU behind a ±2^24 exact-range check) with count, sum, average, minimum, maximum, median and sample deviation; median and deviation sort their rows (96 bytes per row, at most 4,194,304 rows). capabilities.title: SQL Data Explorer
capabilities.foundation: Working DuckDB-WASM panel, explicit source registration, SQL queries and resident native result publication
capabilities.gap: SQL4 (headless WebGPU spec modules/kepler/test/resident-sql-strings-gpu.spec.ts passes; browser script native-sql-gpu.mjs ran 2026-10-31: 33 of 40 fixture queries pass, 7 fail, baseline segment fails on a dataset name, see backlog SQL6-4): Resident datasets are registered with LuSQLContext (resident-sql-gpu-runtime.ts, resident-sql-plan.ts) as borrowed GPU dataframes; filter, global-sort and dense aggregate results are produced on the GPU and adopted with adoptResidentDataset (only row counts and join bound flags are read back; multi-batch sources keep one output chunk per non-empty batch; fixed a bug where batches after the first gathered the wrong rows). Now on the GPU: (1) string predicates over dictionary columns (=, <>, <, <=, >, >=, IN, NOT IN, LIKE, ILIKE, NOT LIKE with prefix/suffix/contains/general patterns and ESCAPE): the pattern is evaluated against the dictionary once on the CPU and a GPU gather by dictionary code builds a 0/1 mask column (resident-sql-strings.ts, resident-sql-derived.ts); string projection by zero-copy dictionary alias (col AS name, CAST(col AS VARCHAR)); GROUP BY a string key; ORDER BY a string sorts by a label-rank lookup unless the dictionary is already in code point order; GROUP BY now drops empty dictionary slots through a COUNT(*) presence column. (2) CAST among int/float/bool with a derived GPU kernel (round half away from zero; NaN, out of range and negative-to-unsigned give null where DuckDB would raise an error; BOOLEAN publishes as 0/1 uint32; BIGINT is 32-bit) and string-to-number per dictionary label (a label that does not parse refuses the statement). (3) joins with right-side columns (INNER, LEFT, RIGHT, FULL, ON a = b or USING, string or integer keys, SQL aliases and select order) run on the resident join executor; duplicateRightMatches all/first/last via -- luma: directives or runtime.setJoinPolicy; colliding right names take rightColumnSuffix. SQL5 (headless WebGPU specs resident-sql-expressions-gpu.spec.ts 6/6 and resident-sql-compose-gpu.spec.ts 4/4 pass; browser fixture script run 2026-10-31: 33 of 40 queries pass, 7 fail): also on the GPU now: BETWEEN / NOT BETWEEN (rewritten to comparisons, numeric, string and date operands); string functions UPPER, LOWER, TRIM/LTRIM/RTRIM (spaces), LENGTH, SUBSTR (positive literal start), REPLACE, CONCAT and || evaluated per dictionary label on the CPU into a new sorted dictionary and gathered by code on the GPU, also inside WHERE/GROUP BY/ORDER BY; expressions over two string columns (a || b, bounded to 65,536 label pairs, otherwise DuckDB with the stated reason; SQL6 lifts the two-column limit, see below); comparing two string columns (=, <>, <, ... through ranks in the shared dictionary); CAST(numeric AS VARCHAR) via a GPU distinct pass (order-preserving key, GPUSort, run flags, GPUScan, compaction; SQL6 raised the limit from 65,536 per chunk to 1,048,576 distinct values over all chunks, labels DuckDB-style, resolved at execution so planning stays synchronous) then a GPU binary-search gather by value; CAST of numeric expressions (+ - * /, unary minus, ABS, FLOOR, CEIL, ROUND, SQRT over numeric columns) through a generated WGSL kernel; CAST to DATE/TIMESTAMP as epoch seconds in an int32 column (strings parsed per label, numeric columns taken as epoch seconds, DATE floors to UTC midnight, string literals compared with such columns become epoch seconds; the column carries luma.gl.time.format=X metadata); joins followed by WHERE, GROUP BY, ORDER BY, LIMIT and expressions (join into a resident intermediate then the normal stages), multi-key ON (up to 4; exact for string keys, exact ranks for numeric keys since SQL6) and SEMI/ANTI joins.  SUBSTR with non-literal or non-positive start, TRIM of non-space characters via column arguments, CAST to BOOLEAN of expressions, CAST of a numeric expression to VARCHAR, CAST to other types (decimal with scale, intervals, nested), DATE/TIMESTAMP with sub-second precision or outside 1901 to 2038, MIN/MAX of strings, ROUND with digits, subqueries and more than two tables in a join, complex CTEs. Differences from DuckDB: out-of-range or NaN CAST gives NULL instead of an error, integer expression overflow wraps, BIGINT is 32-bit, floats are f32, UPPER/LOWER use JavaScript case mapping, whole-join materialization pays the full join output before WHERE/LIMIT. Hidden helper columns are dropped from resident results; the Arrow readback fallback does not drop them (not reachable today). Not done: Kepler SqlPanel/SchemaPanel/PreviewDataPanel not used; a successful GPU run closes the data modal (addDataToMap), so native-sql-gpu.mjs reads GPU results from publications; browser verification of string and join queries ran 2026-10-31 with 33 of 40 fixture queries passing (join-group-order-limit, join-expression, numeric multi-key semi/anti, string-concat-three-columns and two DuckDB window fallbacks fail). SQL6 (headless WebGPU specs resident-sql-expressions-gpu.spec.ts 9/9, resident-sql-compose-gpu.spec.ts 6/6 and resident-sql-strings-gpu.spec.ts pass; node specs for the router, ranked keys and expression planning pass; no browser run): (1) CAST to DATE/TIMESTAMP columns now reach Kepler as timestamp fields: executeDataframe reads the epoch-second column back (8 bytes per row, reserved up front) into exact int64 second time words and adoptResidentDataset(timeColumns) uploads them beside the scalar column, so the dataset has a real native time field (TimeRuntime, time filter, time charts) while SQL, tooltips and the table keep the sint32 seconds with format X; source-publication.ts types the field timestamp with format 'X' for resident results (browser not verified). (2) A numeric CAST to VARCHAR no longer has a 65,536-per-chunk cap: chunks are sorted one after another and the merged dictionary may hold 1,048,576 distinct values; beyond that, and for empty results and data-dependent join limits (output over uint32, non-integral Float32 keys, ranking that does not fit), execution throws SqlExecutionRefusal and the explorer router (runSqlWithFallback in sql-backend-router.ts) retries the same statement on DuckDB, showing the reason beside the Arrow-transfer notice. (3) Numeric multi-key LEFT/RIGHT/FULL/SEMI/ANTI joins and every duplicate policy run exactly: at execution a GPU distinct pass over both sides ranks each numeric key column (rank tables in resident-join-composite-rank.ts), keys fold into the mixed radix with string components, and the unchanged executor emits matched and unmatched rows. If the radix product exceeds 32 bits or a column has more than 1,048,576 distinct keys, INNER joins with every duplicate match and equal key types fall back to the hashed key plus the exact residual, anything else is refused to DuckDB. (4) ANTI JOIN may select right columns (NULL on every kept row, as in DuckDB); SEMI JOIN right columns stay refused because DuckDB's binder rejects them too. String functions and || over three to eight dictionary columns run as one mixed-radix label lookup while the product of the dictionary sizes is at most 65,536 (two columns per pass beyond the shader binding limit); a larger product still goes to DuckDB with the reason. Also fixed a SQL5 planner bug where a || inside a function call (UPPER(a || b)) produced overlapping rewrites and failed. Remaining on DuckDB: string expressions whose dictionary product exceeds 65,536 or with more than eight columns (no per-row GPU string builder, no observed-combination path), non-equality or extra right-side predicates in ON, subqueries and EXISTS/IN semi joins, more than two tables, CROSS JOIN, MIN/MAX of strings, sub-second or out-of-range time values. Time columns hold whole epoch seconds in 1901 to 2038. DATA4: exact 64-bit COUNT/SUM/MIN/MAX statements over Int64/Uint64 columns (optional integer WHERE) run on the exact wide-numeric kernels instead of the Float32 route and return exact values (decimal text beyond Int32); GPU spec verified, no browser run.
